newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas seen higher on power price surge.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas seen higher on power price surge.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Monday on the strength of a surge in spot electricity prices due to nuclear generation unit outages, industry sources said.
July Henry Hub gas was seen at $2.27-2.29 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) in early over the counter discussion from Friday's NYMEX July futures settlement at $2.235 per mmBtu.
"Electricity prices are screaming, and because electricity is up gas is going up as well," said gas futures trader.
Day-ahead electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. surged almost $20.00 Monday from Friday's levels on news of two unplanned nuclear plant outages in Pennsylvania, market sources said.

Firm, peak electricity for Tuesday in Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool was quoted Monday at $42.00-44.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), easing slightly after trades as high as $46.00, brokers and traders said.
PECO Energy's 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 1 nuclear power unit, in Pottstown, Pa., was shut Saturday to repair leaking safety relief valves. It is expected to stay shut through most of the week.
GPU Nuclear's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 nuclear power station in Londonderry Township, Pa., tripped off line Saturday after it lost offsite power.
Three Mile Island 1 was expected to stay shut at least until midweek.

These latest outages, added to long-term outages at the two nuclear power units at the Salem, New Jersey facility, account for 4,053 MW, or about 31 percent of PJM's total 12,833 MW nuclear baseload generating capability.
Air conditioning demand was expected to be strong through much of the week in the PJM area.
On Friday, July Henry Hub gas firmed 1.4 cents, boosted by a late wave of pre-weekend short covering.
